chief_complaint: burning pain, shiny blue skin, swelling in hand post-cast
hpi_details: A 53-year-old male presents to the clinic with burning pain, shiny blue skin, swelling in hand post-cast. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks his cast was wrapped way too tightly and cut off the blood supply or caused a deep bone infection in his hand.
concerns: He is terrified that the purplish color and burning pain mean gangrene is setting in and his hand will have to be amputated.
expectations: He hopes to get strong pain medication so he can tolerate touching his hand and an ultrasound scan to make sure there is no blood clot.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Management requires confirmation of the clinical diagnosis and exclusion of infection, vascular compromise, and other causes. Early graded functional use, desensitization, and rehabilitation are central; medication or procedures require individualized specialist assessment.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Complex Regional Pain Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe progressive motor deficit.
management_principles: Exclude infection, vascular compromise, and other mimics before treatment; use graded functional rehabilitation and desensitization when tolerated.

Refer promptly to pain or rehabilitation specialists for diagnostic uncertainty, severe functional limitation, or inadequate progress; consider medication or sympathetic blocks only after individualized assessment.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: When did this pain start compared to your fracture and the time your cast was removed?
Is the pain a burning sensation, and does it get triggered by something as light as air or fabric touching your skin?
Have you noticed your hand changing color, like turning blue or red, or feeling colder than the other side?
Has the hand been swollen, or have you noticed changes in your skin, hair, or nail growth?
How much is this affecting your ability to move or use your hand for daily tasks?

history.answer: Ever since my cast was removed, my right hand has been burning intensely, swelling up, and turning a shiny bluish color.
I noticed the swelling and a mild burning feeling right after my cast was taken off two weeks ago, and it has become steadily worse each day.
The burning pain covers my entire right hand, from my wrist all the way into the tips of my fingers, without radiating up into my neck or shoulder.
It feels like a constant, scorching fire or severe sunburn on my hand, and I would rate the severity around an 8 out of 10.
Even the slightest brush of my shirt sleeve or a cool breeze across my hand triggers unbearable agony.
I slipped on ice about eight weeks ago and fractured my right wrist, so I was in a short arm cast for six weeks until it was removed two weeks ago.
My hand looks purplish-blue and shiny compared to my normal hand, and it often feels unusually sweaty and cooler to the touch.
The whole hand is puffy, especially around the back of my hand and knuckles, and the skin looks stretched and glossy.
My fingers feel extremely stiff, and I can barely bend them into a loose fist because of the tightness and burning.
Moving my fingers, touching anything, or letting the hand hang down makes the throbbing and burning much worse, and keeping it gently elevated gives only slight relief.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, there are no open sores, cuts, drainage, or pus coming from my hand.
No, my fingers are not pale, white, or suddenly paralyzed, although they are very stiff and painful to move.
Yes, I have been feeling worn out and fatigued lately, mostly because the continuous burning pain keeps waking me up at night.
I cannot use my right hand to type, hold a mug, or get dressed, and the relentless pain makes it almost impossible to sleep through the night.
history.topic: Impact on daily life and sleep

history.answer: No, I have never experienced anything like this burning pain or swelling before in my life.
I tried taking over-the-counter ibuprofen and acetaminophen, but they hardly took the edge off the burning.
I think that cast was put on way too tightly and ended up cutting off the blood flow or causing an infection in the bone.
Looking at how purple and swollen my hand is, I'm terrified that gangrene is setting in and they're going to have to take my hand off.
I just want some strong pain medicine so I can bear having my hand touched, and a scan to check for a blood clot.
I have always been healthy with no history of high blood pressure, diabetes, or nerve problems.
I had an uncomplicated appendectomy twenty years ago, and I have never had any other surgeries or hospitalizations.
I am not taking any regular prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I have a glass of beer once or twice a month at social gatherings, nothing more.
I work as an office accountant and live with my wife and teenage daughter in an apartment.
There is no family history of chronic pain syndromes, autoimmune disorders, or vascular diseases.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 125/80 mmHg, pulse 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Alert, middle-aged male in mild distress, protectively guarding his right forearm and cradling his right hand against his chest.
Right hand and wrist demonstrate diffuse non-pitting swelling, shiny tight skin with bluish-mottled discoloration, and increased sweating compared to the normal left hand.
Marked allodynia and hyperalgesia to light touch with a cotton swab and pinprick over the dorsum and palm of the right hand without a single dermatomal cut-off.
Diffuse tenderness across the right wrist and metacarpophalangeal joints with severely restricted active and passive finger flexion and extension due to severe burning pain.
Right hand grip and finger extension are severely reduced secondary to pain and stiffness, while proximal upper limb strength is preserved at 5/5.
Radial and ulnar pulses are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally, with capillary refill under 2 seconds in all fingertips.
No palpable epitrochlear, axillary, or cervical lymphadenopathy.
